quest.title: Ripples That Will Never Reach
quest.description: After reaching an understanding, you decide to head back to the Silvermoon Hall to ask around about what kind of gifts Columbina likes.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1425, Primogem x30, Mora x62225, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act V
chapter.title: A Nocturne of the Far North

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Columbina! We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh. She's not here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't sense her presence at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weren't there a few kuuhenki here last time, too? Where did they all go?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe she took them out for walkies?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Walkies? For kuuhenki? They're not pets, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh well, looks like we just came at a bad time. Let's try again tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's still a few days until Moon-Prayer Night, so we're in no rush. Besides, she needs time to rest anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fair point. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Columbina? Are you back yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. How strange. Looks like she still isn't here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a bit odd...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right? It's not like her to spend so much time outside. Especially since she's worried about attracting unwanted attention.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: By the looks of it, she hasn't been back all day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about Luonnotar? Luonnotar, you there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Do you know where Columbina went?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Sorry, didn't understand. But if you know where she is, could you take us to her?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like an "I don't know either" to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... That's even stranger...

choices.text: Paimon, look...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about 'em? Oh... That's not good news...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They change color when Columbina gets weaker, right? And they look super pale right now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go. We've got to find Lauma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea. She might know what's happening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lauma!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Ah, it's you. How is Kuutar? Is she okay?

choices.text: She's missing.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No, she hasn't... I came here to check on her after I noticed the flowers had changed color.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Based on past precedent, she must be very weak right now. Even getting up to walk would be a struggle... it seems unlikely that she wandered off outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not to mention that she doesn't do that at the best of times, either. So yeah, this is super weird.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Has anyone approached Silvermoon Hall lately?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No. Very few people are in the know about Kuutar's whereabouts. And if anyone suspicious had visited, they'd have left some sort of evidence.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Come on, let's go to Nasha Town. If anyone has seen her, someone there will know about it. It's Nod-Krai's information hub after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Makes sense. Let's go!

choices.text: Has she visited the Frostmoon Scions?
The flowers...

talks.objective: Go to Nasha Town to collect intel

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a moment... Is it just Paimon, or is this stall kinda suspicious? It's never been here before, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: No... I don't recognize it...
Mwahahaha! Alas, your free-and-easy adventure time is over. Now, prepare to face the final boss of Nod-Krai!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where'd that voice come from?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Not sure, but it's definitely hostile...
No, no, no, not that way! The final boss is right here.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The... Sniffer Mole?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the final boss? Surely not. Also...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That voice is a little familiar.
Hahaha, okay, the jig is up. I'll stop teasing you. Turn around — I'm right behind you.
It seems I've managed to leave quite an indelible impression, even though you've never seen my face... Ah, nothing could make a great mage more pleased with herself.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Wh—What is going on...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I've heard that all the big shots of Teyvat have long, wordy titles that stun people speechless when they make their entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, none of them are affiliated with the Hexenzirkel, and we ourselves keep a very low profile... The notorious name-dropping doesn't quite work for us. Still, I for one think I'm really quite amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: So that didn't stop me from coming up with a title anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alice? It's really you this time! Not a lantern, or a Dodoco... but Alice in the flesh!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: That's right! So, what do you think? How does it feel to finally meet me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You look like...

choices.text: You look just like Klee!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Aha! That's the first thing you thought? A little surprising, but that actually makes me very happy.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Because that means that when Klee grows up, she'll be just as stunningly beautiful as her mother!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: So, she's a... friend of yours?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Kind of? This is actually the first time we've seen her in person.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I see. Madame Mage, that was, uh... quite a powerful entrance. I certainly won't be forgetting it any time soon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, Lauma, don't force it. Paimon will do the honors. This is Alice from the Hexenzirkel. She's a friend of ours, and of Varka's too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She's helped us a lot in the past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! She's a good person, just kinda... unpredictable.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Well, what is the human heart if not unpredictable, hmm? If we could not do as we please, how would we differ from machines?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I am Lauma, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions. It is a pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh, I know, I know. Before you got here, I spent a good, oh, 15 minutes getting up to speed on Nod-Krai's present situation.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In other words, I've read the whole "in the last episode" part, so we can skip the pleasantries.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Fair enough. Well, Ms. Alice, I can already tell that you have quite a unique personality.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You'll get used to it. Paimon sure is... So anyway, what are you doing in Nod-Krai, Alice?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh? I thought I told you already? This time, I'm the final boss.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And what a formidable foe I shall be! Powerful, confident, decisive! And good luck finding my weak spot — you will never succeed!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm going to send a formal request for Jean to put you in solitary.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: *gasp* Ah! Drat! My one weakness, and you found it in an instant! Fate has been dealt a devastating blow...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Thus falls the great Dodo-King!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uh, why are you playing along with this nonsense?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: For funsies, of course! What's wrong, Paimon? Are you disappointed in me? Am I a gigantic let-down?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, it's just... You seem like a busy lady, and this is the one time you've shown up in person. Paimon figured it would be for something more high-stakes than just goofing around...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: You're quite right. I'm here in Nod-Krai because something big happened. Something big enough that it caught the attention of the Hexenzirkel.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It concerns the three moons, Teyvat's borders, and of course, the Moon Goddess you are currently searching for.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know where Columbina is?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Kind of. Why don't we discuss this over a pot of tea?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: My main reason for coming on this trip to Teyvat was, of course, to have some fun. But I do technically have a job to do as well — namely, maintaining the stability of Teyvat's borders.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I'll skip over the complicated parts, but to sum it up, Abyssal energies are all that lie beyond Teyvat's border. We'd find ourselves in a real pickle if they ever made it through.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And the phantoms you've been seeing are a sign that the border has been disturbed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, no wonder they tend to show up around Moon-Prayer Night...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Is it because the real moon is now so close to us that its power can cross the border?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In part. But only a negligible amount passes through — just enough to influence the Verdant Crests and so on.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And as you've noticed, there has been an unprecedented number of phantoms appearing this year. The influence of the moon beyond the border cannot explain this. No, there is another, far greater factor at play...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The "Trilunar Syzygy."

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: A Trilunar... Syzygy...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Eons ago, before the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat, it was the then-three Moon Goddesses who controlled the laws of this world.

choices.text: You're talking about...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: That's exactly it. The three goddesses split these powers amongst themselves, promising never to consolidate them into one singular body. This was meant to keep the world stable.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But fast-forwarding to the present, the Eternal Moon's Marrow is with you, while the Iridescent Moon's Marrow — which should never have appeared in this world — has been retrieved. Add that to the presence of a Moon Goddess in the flesh, and...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The power of all three moons is gathered here in Nod-Krai. There hasn't been an event like this since the war of funerary flame.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And it's having a noticeable effect on Teyvat's borders.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why are you so concerned about said borders, if I might ask?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Because... I wish to give my darling daughter a peaceful, sunny environment to grow up in. Is that a good enough reason?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kinda sounds like you're dodging the question... but it does make sense.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Well, that's one reason, anyway. And the most important one. The others are a little complicated to explain — for instance, cleaning up after dearest Miss "R"...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Albedo can tell you more about that if you're curious. But right now, I have a more important question to ask you: Why are you collecting the Moon Marrows?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Columbina wants to use their power to return home.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I see, I see. Nicole told me about that legend once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: N—Nicole!? You mean Mage "N"?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh, so you remember.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We heard her voice in Fontaine...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ah yes, of course. That was a story about "fate" — her area of expertise.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But back to the story of our dear Moon Goddess... I'm afraid her intended method of returning to the moon is unlikely to work anymore.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: What does that mean?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: She may be missing... but she hasn't "gone" anywhere. She has... disappeared.

choices.text: Life, "Death," and such, aren't you?
You look so young!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: What is that supposed to mean, hmm? Hmm? I'm the mother of Klee, Teyvat's number one cutie. How old could I possibly be?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My body is so... heavy...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Wait, no. It's... my mind that's heavy. My arms and legs are as light as a feather...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (What's... happening to me? I feel... drowsy, like I've been asleep for too long... Is it daytime or nighttime? Is the moon out?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Phew... I think I'll go for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Have I grown so weak that... I can't even sustain my physical form?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But Moon-Prayer Night is nearly here... I was so close to returning home...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Death is near... Is this how it ends for me...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Will I return to the moon after I disappear? Or...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I don't want it to end like this.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (So far, at least, I still exist — even if not physically. I can still feel...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (But as my power wanes, I'm sure that, too, will fade...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I suppose... I might take one final look at this world. The world where I was born.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I'm seeing so much that I'd never usually get to see... They'd never act like this when I was around.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Mmm... It's nice, being able to just watch people in peace in these final moments...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #What a rare opportunity. I think I'll go take a look around in Nasha Town, too. Maybe {NICKNAME} will be there...

dialogues.speaker: Lemetti
dialogues.text: ...Hahahaha! Come on, come on!

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: ...Wait for meeee!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Frostmoon Enclave... How much it has changed since I was born...

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: These decorations... they're so heavy!

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: It's times like this when you kinda wish men could be priestesses and acolytes too...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (How fascinating... I've never had the chance to be privy to people's private lives in this way.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (In the past, people would get so solemn and serious the moment I showed my face... like they were frozen stiff.)

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Kaarina! Lemetti! It's time to eat!

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: Coming!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...I want to watch them a little longer.)

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: I'm sure you're both tired from playing all day! Come on, eat up.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...A plain, humble meal. That has always been the way of the Frostmoon Scions.)

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: Huh? How come Lemetti got a Midsommar Berry dessert? I always get Lakkaberry...

dialogues.speaker: Lemetti
dialogues.text: Umm... I don't mind sharing! You can have a bite of mine if I get to have a bite of yours?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Hmm? They're sharing food?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I've never shared food with anyone before... Even at the Harbinger tea parties, everyone just ate off their own plate...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (And when I couldn't finish my food offerings from the Frostmoon Scions, they'd leave the leftovers out under the moonlight for the animals to claim...)

dialogues.speaker: Lemetti
dialogues.text: Hey! That was two bites!

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Then you can have another bite of mine!

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Oh, you two...

dialogues.speaker: Sarakka
dialogues.text: Don't fret, now. Here, have some of Granny's, too.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hehe... So this is what it means to be "family"?

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: ...So just, fill these balloons with air, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Yep. Try a couple now to test things out — the rest can wait till Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: ...Hehehe.

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: Think fast!

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Aah!

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Reettaaaa!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Teasing an acolyte of the Frostmoon Scions? Surely that's a punishable offense...)

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Take THIS!

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: Ahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Heh! Alright, enough horsing around. Lady Lauma gave us a task — we should get back to it.

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: The task is just to check that the balloons don't leak, right? Doesn't matter if we fill them with air or water. Hi-yah!

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Oof! Okay, you got me there... Aaand you got me there. But still, we can't use all the balloons before the festival even starts.

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: We won't use ALL of them... And as long as Lady Lauma's trusted acolyte doesn't snitch, this can stay as a little secret between friends. A couple more can't do any harm, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zirnytsia
dialogues.text: Oh, you menace... Then THINK FAST!

dialogues.speaker: Reetta
dialogues.text: Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Is pumping a balloon full of water really so much fun?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You should get going. It's important that we ascertain what Kuutar likes.

talks.objective: Think about what to do next

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: After the war of funerary flame, the Moon Goddesses were no longer recognized by Teyvat. They lost the whole foundation for their existence.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: That's why the Moon Goddess's strength is fading. She cannot withstand the world's rejection of her.

choices.text: It's just like what Columbina said...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: To be more pedantic about it, the Moon Goddesses did something to offend the Heavenly Principles, and that's why they were ousted. Something of a recurring theme in Teyvat's history.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Theoretically, speaking so candidly should put me in their crosshairs, too — but they can't tell me what to do. I'll say whatever I want.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Anywho, the Moon Marrow energies were but a drop in the bucket for her, and that battle against the Rächer of Solnari only weakened her further.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Fortunately, it happened close enough to Moon-Prayer Night, when the kuuvahki concentration here is high. That's the only reason she's managed to survive this long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean, "fortunately"? You said she disappeared... We're too late...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ugh, what a headache — I thought this was all common knowledge. I guess I have some more explaining to do... Okay, buckle up, it's time for another lecture.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Now, I said earlier that the Moon Goddesses lost the foundation for their existence.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The reason for that has to do with the natural order. Basically, the rationale for their existence in Teyvat was lost.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The same logic applies to the present Moon Goddess, too. Consider her existence so far. Her comrades in the Fatui called her "Damselette"...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And she was worshiped as Kuutar by the Frostmoon Scions. But these connections have now been severed, whether by her hand or yours.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: So the "rationale" that once sustained her existence is now gone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... we did that to her!?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Well, strictly speaking... yes, but let's not start pointing fingers, shall we? I'll only end up as the big bad villain, and that's not the kind of final boss I want to be!

choices.text: If you're making light of this...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Of course I do! I'm only the greatest mage in the whole entire world!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Now, if you wish to find your Moon Goddess, there are two problems we need to solve.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Firstly, we'll need to strengthen the connection between her and Teyvat, at least enough to sustain her until Moon-Prayer Night.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Strengthen her connection... But... does that mean I'll have to rally all the Frostmoon faithful behind this?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I'm afraid a bygone faith and a former home won't be of any help to her now. Hmm... Do you know her name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Her... name?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Yes. Names are very important things. A name is a fundamental concept that anchors one's entire existence.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I asked her once, but she said she didn't know.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Then your first job is to find it. As a Moon Goddess, I'm sure she must have a name she identifies with.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Neither "Columbina" nor "Kuutar" is her true name, and she's never really accepted either of them.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: So... finding out her real name is enough to sustain her existence?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Yes. I know it sounds like a small step, but every journey begins that way. So for now, that's all we need to focus on.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The second problem is with her plan to use the Moon Marrows to return to the moon. Unfortunately, piercing through the false sky will take an enormous amount of power.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Given her current condition, she won't be able to provide anywhere near enough power — even if she recovers her physical form.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But, no need to fret. Nicole's the expert in this field, and I'm sure she'll figure something out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Mage "N" is going to help us out, too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means we've got two Hexenzirkel mages on the case... This is turning into a pretty big deal!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Mm... Actually, this is more of a side quest for me. Hehe.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Like you said, I'm a busy lady, so I can't stay for too long. I'll have to return to Teyvat's border soon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for telling us all of this.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Haha, that's the upside you get for looking out for my little Klee! Hopefully that will incentivize you to carry on keeping her company in the future~

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Anyway, jokes aside, you'd better get moving. It will take quite a miracle for the Moon Goddess's consciousness to hold out till Moon-Prayer Night.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh! And I suppose I might as well tell you where Nicole is before I leave.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Off you go, now! Time to meet your new friend. Ah yes, and a little suggestion — don't forget to... mind your heads.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... What?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hmm, I wonder how Durin's doing? I should really go see him before I head back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You really are super busy.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: *sigh* I most certainly am! There's so many children I have to keep tabs on just in Mondstadt. Durin, Albedo, Venti, Varka...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There were some unexpected names in there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Klee didn't make the list, huh?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Of course not. Klee is my pride and joy. I have no qualms about her, because she's the best child in the whole wide world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Uh, yep! Klee's a little angel, mm-hmm...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I'm glad you agree. Well, all the best! See you when I see you~

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: She left in a hurry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, she didn't pack up her stall. Should we handle it for her?

choices.text: I doubt that's necessary.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I must say, I'm now very curious about her daughter... Klee, wasn't it? What's she like?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's... a long story. Come on, we'll fill you in as we go.

choices.text: A mage of her abilities doesn't need our help.
Hopefully that means you have a plan?
The world itself is rejecting her...

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: ...Hey, have you decided what to give her for Moon-Prayer Night?

dialogues.speaker: Domovoj
dialogues.text: I sure have! Hehe, she's gonna get the surprise of her life when she's least expecting it! Then I'll whip out the ring and pop the question...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ("The surprise of her life"... What a fun turn of phrase.)

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Cool, I get the picture. You can spare me the gushy details... Oh! Looks like we have a customer.

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Hello there, Ma'am. Would you like some Moon-Prayer Night candy?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is he... talking to me? Can he see me?)

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Here you go!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Limppu
dialogues.text: Come back any time! Right, now where were we...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I don't know why but... I still held out hope...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...The most important thing right now is to find that mage...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...This name thing seems super important too. But where do we even start looking?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...I'd better go pay the Fatui a visit...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go. This is no time to be spacing out.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (What a lively place. I've never experienced Nasha Town like this before.)

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: Hey, you old geezer. Your hammer's rusted through!

dialogues.speaker: Arkhyp
dialogues.text: Who are you calling "old geezer"?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Are they... quarreling?)

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: I'm lookin' right at him! You've really gone downhill since giving your daughter free reign in the workshop. Can you even swing a hammer anymore? It shouldn't take you days just to fix a single chair!

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: You might as well use that hammer to massage my back, for all the good it's doing!

dialogues.speaker: Arkhyp
dialogues.text: Heh, don't run your mouth, or you'll get a back massage that'll put you in bed for the rest of your life! Look, the materials haven't arrived yet, alright? You know how busy it gets in the days before Moon-Prayer Night!

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: I'll bet you sent all the materials to your little princess. *sigh* Blood's always thicker than water, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lyulka
dialogues.text: Alright, you've made your point, Uncle Koski. As soon as the materials arrive, fixing your chair will be the number one priority. And dad, if you've got time to chat, why don't you lend me a hand, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: See? Lyulka knows what the score is.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I guess they're... friends? But the way they spoke to each other was so ugly.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Then again... It wouldn't be the first time I've seen something like this...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbinaaaa! Sing outside my door in the middle of the night one more time and I'll unscrew your vocal cords! You hear me?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh... Sandrone...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (So that was her way of trying to be friends with me?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What a pity... I won't get the chance to say any ugly things in reply...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Where are they going? They mentioned a "mage" and... a name?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So, Mr. Varka, are you acquainted with this Nicole? Or should I call her Mage "N"?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ah, not really. We've never met, though she has come up in conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: From what I've gathered, Alice kinda took Nicole under her wing. Taught her how to speak in a more ladylike fashion, that kind of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Hard to imagine Alice as an etiquette coach...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha! Yeah, Alice is a larger-than-life personality, I'll give you that. But then again, that's why she's able to draw such an eclectic mix of people into her inner circle.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: If I remember correctly, being an "interesting" person is actually one of her main entry requirements. Heh, so if you ever wanted to join the Hexenzirkel, I'm sure you'd both be eligible to apply.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't go around making promises on Alice's behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I wouldn't dare! I'm just... trying to paint a picture of the Hexenzirkel for you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, sure. Anyway, since none of us have ever met Nicole, how are we supposed to find her? We can't just go up to every woman in sight and ask, "Hey, are you Nicole?"

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hmm, maybe something she's wearing will give it away? Like, uh, a Windblume pinned to her chest, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. Alice never said Nicole was from Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Oh, true.

choices.text: What about a tea set?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That would be... this young lady, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey there, sorry to disturb you, but... are you Ms. Nicole?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Varka, Knight of Boreas of the Knights of Favonius. Alice might have mentioned me before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Have we got the wrong person? Sorry, sorry!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Well, this is awkward...)
When I shook my head, I meant "no, Alice hasn't mentioned you before."

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Huh? Where is this voice coming from...?
My apologies. For certain reasons, I am unable to speak. This is the only way I can communicate with you.
It might take some getting used to, but I hope you can understand.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hey, it's fine... I'm more shocked by the fact that Alice never speaks about me! Hahaha.
As for you two... We have crossed paths twice before, but it is nonetheless a pleasure to finally meet you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's really you! Thanks for all your guidance in the past...
You're quite welcome. This time, things are different... We have reached the unwritten pages of the story. You might say that we stand at the crossroads of fate...
Now, then. Allow me to formally introduce myself. My name is—
No no no, stop, I...! Ugh, Alice! I can't believe it...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: I had a whole speech prepared! I'd agonized over every single word! ...She always picks the worst moments to ruin other people's plans...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: I'm so sorry about that... Alice took the liberty of devising some bespoke "Self Introduction Magic" for each member of the Hexenzirkel...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But I could've sworn I deleted all of the triggering conditions for it. How did it bypass everything? ...Oh gosh, this is so embarrassing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (This is a very different side of Nicole than what we're used to... Is she... not used to face-to-face interactions?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, d—don't worry about it. We've seen that introduction magic once already, so it wasn't too much of a shock.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Please go on, Ms. Nicole. We'd love to hear what you have to... say, or... well, communicate.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (Huh? Are they talking to this lady? But...)

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Will you all promise to forget that horrendously embarrassing introduction?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sorry? Embarrassing? When?

choices.text: Among the words that hopped out just now, I saw...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Yes. My name is Nicole, and I am one of a very few angels who have retained both their preferred form and their power.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon should be no strangers to this concept. There is another of our kind in Natlan — they call her the Lord of the Night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, right, Paimon remembers her!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But we've never seen her in person.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes, well, I have retained more of my power than she. It's because I don't have a long-term duty to fulfill. To be more specific...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Ah, no, we'll be here all day if I get into the specifics. Moving on. If I'm not mistaken... you are here because you wish to learn how one might reach the moon beyond the sky.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That's right. Is that something you can give us any guidance on?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes, I do know a way. It began with the Hyperboreans who lived after the war of funerary flame... Hmm. Blank looks. Maybe I should start with the background of the war...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Or maybe not. It shouldn't be an issue. I'll fill in the gaps for you when we have more time. Anyway, after that war ended, the three moons retreated to beyond the false sky.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The Hyperboreans were humans I once aided. They accepted the civilization and creations bestowed upon them by the angels.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But despite accepting many blessings of the angels, many among them still held onto their faith in the moons. They were reluctant to accept the new order.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Even after the war of funerary flame, they sought to contact the moon goddesses beyond the sky and receive their guidance...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But all three had passed away by that point.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (This mage has a unique method of communicating... Is she talking about the moons?)

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes, but they did not know. And so, still they prayed for the Moon Goddesses' mercy.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: After building titanic structures that consumed vast amounts of kuuvahki, at last they glimpsed the moons and heard their voices...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But of course, they were gravely disappointed. For it was then that they realized: the three moon goddesses were dead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's such a sad story...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It is. Humanity was in a very sorry state at that time. The angels who had once aided them were gone, and the war of funerary flames had left them homeless and destitute...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Just a second. I gotta ask... How relevant is all this history to the task at hand...?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Well, I mean, it's... Hmm. Okay, it seems we've drifted into irrelevant narrative waters.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It's been a while since I've had the chance to speak inside someone's head. As soon as I got started, I lost control, and the words just flowed out like a waterfall...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...What I'm trying to say is... Right, yes, that's it: The relevant part is the ritual created by the Hyperboreans.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The fact that they bypassed the false sky and saw the true moons implies that they successfully built a connection between Teyvat and the outside world.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Which means, with enough kuuvahki and a sufficiently stable connection, it should be feasible to send one person over the border.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... so they built some kinda portal?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Oh, uh... Yes, a portal. Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Is something wrong? You sound... disappointed.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: I just didn't expect you to summarize it so well... It turns out I could have said all that in one word, if only I'd managed to think of it.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No, please, it's fine. This is invaluable knowledge. I'll be sure to record and preserve everything in writing.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Oh, really? Well in that case, I suppose I could backtrack and add some more detail. I did gloss over a few things so far...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa. Timeout. Let's summarize what we've got first!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The Hyperboreans were the last ones to use this method, right? So we somehow need to find whatever structure they built and make sure there's enough kuuvahki to power it up.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Luckily, we have the moon marrow of both the Eternal and Iridescent Moons, so we're all good for kuuvahki. Which means, the key issue we need to focus on is finding the place. Am I right so far?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes, although I expect the structure is long gone by now.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: That said, what if we could take advantage of the phantoms to travel back to a time when it still existed?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Well, "travel back" isn't quite accurate. It's more like we'd be creating a handshake between two points in spacetime.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: We wouldn't even have to pick a time when it still existed — it could just be a time when it still appeared in phantom form via projection. Or, we could project our own phantoms, fold them together, and...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...You look lost. Was that too hard to follow?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, things got a little, uh, technical there. Paimon's brain is reaching capacity...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Alright, let me think about how to put this more simply... Okay, got it.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Over the next few days, I'll search for phantoms that we can use. Once I find one that meets the criteria, I'll let you know and we'll regroup.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: By completing certain rituals, specific individuals will be able to enter the phantom and make it to the Hyperborean structure.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: If everything checks out, and it looks feasible, we'll just need to wait for Moon-Prayer Night and we can send the Moon Goddess back home... I'm really skimping on the detail here. Is this making any sense at all?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I think so. For now, we'll just wait to hear from you.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes... Basically, yes.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Great. Counting on you! In the meantime, we'll focus on finding the Moon Goddess's name.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (...! My... name? Are they... looking for a way to stop me from disappearing?)

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Excuse me, Miss...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Go on, Ms. Nicole.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: This conversation was a little all over the place. I didn't catch your name.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I am Lauma, of the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Ah, I did wonder. I noticed that you listened very intently when I spoke about Hyperborea and the moons' history.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: If you'd be interested, I'd love to visit you this evening and go through it again in greater detail.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Also, if you were serious about making a record... It would be too risky to simply write down the raw details as-is. I would suggest some tweaks — maybe rewrite the stories as fairy tales or fables, perhaps even prayers.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Anyway, we can cross that bridge when we come to it. So, see you later, then? Oh, and no need to prepare anything. Just a cup of tea will do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—See ya...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: She seems friendly... it's just...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Ah, it's so nice to find someone who's actually willing to listen! I've been dying for a chance to finally go through all this systematically, from start to finish... Any longer and I'd probably start forgetting it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now Paimon gets why Alice told us to mind our heads...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hahaha, what did I tell you? Lotta quirky people in Alice's orbit.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Now then, the next order of business is: Where do we start looking for the Moon Goddess's name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Maybe the rest of what Nicole has to say might give us some clues.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Once I've heard her out, I'll summarize the salient points and share them with you all.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I'm also inclined to review our other documents. Yes, our faith was first established by our Hyperborean ancestors...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But many of the more factually accurate records are from after Kuutar's birth.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a hunch that the Fatui might know something, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like we're gonna follow Columbina's journey through Teyvat, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, we'll start by heading to the Frostmoon Enclave.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sounds like a plan. Take this with you — I'll see about getting in touch with the Fatui... it'll probably just be Arlecchino and Sandrone again. They're the only ones who would wanna help.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Thank you, Mr. Varka.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hahaha, don't mention it. Honestly, I'm more comfortable dealing with the Fatui than prying into the details of a young lady's childhood. Catch you later!

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (I should follow them, just in case there's some way that I can help...)

choices.text: Angel.
I recall that each mage has their own cup.

talks.objective: Search for information in the Frostmoon Enclave

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: A while ago, I took the time to organize all documents in our possession that pertain to Kuutar. What you see here is the material I consider reliable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're saying, there's unreliable material too?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. Most of the information we have was transmitted through an oral tradition. Inevitably, some of her stories were mythologized and deified over the years through countless retellings. That's why I organized them into reliable and unreliable.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: There is no sense seeking answers in history unless we can ensure the veracity of the historical record.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Makes sense. Alright, let's take a look through.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Clear and concise would be one way to describe the writing style of these historical records. But you could just as easily describe them as "terse and dry."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And since Lauma already knows the material like the back of her hand, the quest to find any new information in these texts is tough going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Almost all these records refer to "Kuutar" instead of "Columbina"... Hmm, although neither of those is her real name... Paimon's not sure what point she's trying to make.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What we can gather from these records is that the Frostmoon Scions worshiped her as a god, placing impossible expectations upon her...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I cannot fault them for their earnest faith. But for all their devotion, worshiping her day in, day out changed nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I imagine that none of it resonated with Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It wouldn't surprise me if even back then, she had already begun to reject the name "Kuutar" and everything it represented...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Lauma speaks the truth.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (When I heard them call upon "Kuutar" with hope and expectation in their voices... They may as well have been calling upon somebody else.)

choices.text: When you were organizing these texts...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Well... That's a bit complicated. I looked at the level of detail, perceived authenticity, prose style...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: And how realistic their portrayal of Kuutar seemed to be.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Amongst the Frostmoon Scions of today, only I know of her existence, and I alone have spoken to her face-to-face. As such, I know that there are certain things she simply would never do.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That being said, I have sensed some changes in her lately.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (...Changes? Me?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, seems like this is getting us nowhere... For what it's worth, why don't we check the "unreliable" sources too?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Sure. Give me a moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exerting but a fraction of her divine might, Kuutar sheared a great mass from the snow-capped mountain and cast it into the sea, upon whose surface shone the mirror image of the moon. Thus was formed the island of Hiisi.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, right... That doesn't even begin to pass the sniff test!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The three moons are naught but lies through and through. Only one moon has ever shone for us, and 'Kuutar' is her name.

choices.text: The subjectivity is strong in this one...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The vast majority of ancient texts are filled with fanciful tales like these. I trust you understand my criteria a little better now.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Kuutar did not speak, merely gazing into the distance in silence. And where her gaze landed, this was her prophecy.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Clearly, whoever wrote this text never even met Kuutar — otherwise, they'd know that her eyes are always closed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What about you, {NICKNAME}? What are you reading?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Seems like a collection of anecdotes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, let Paimon see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The child wished to build a wooden nest with which to shield the fledgling bird from the cold. But being so young and lacking in strength, the child could not snap the branches from the trees...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kuutar was passing by. Upon seeing the child, she summoned forth a kuuhenki, who built a beautiful nest for the child.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Ah, I remember that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not knowing the meaning of Kuutar's divine intervention, the child dared not to respond, and thus ran home to call their parents. But Kuutar was gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Moonchanter declared the event a miracle and took the nest as a relic, placing it on high for all to see. The child was named as one favored by the goddess, and was greatly respected amongst the people...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yet, no further miracles were bestowed, and this matter was forgotten in but a few years.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh. Any thoughts after reading that, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: If it's true...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Columbina probably just wanted to join the kid in making nests...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Ah... I had originally considered this a fabrication, because Kuutar did not perform any similar actions in subsequent records...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But now that I think about it, it does seem like something Columbina would do. It's just that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She didn't know how other people would interpret her actions. She was probably worried about making things difficult for people... and so, she gradually stopped joining in...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's so sad.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: And now, I can make no such gestures of warmth even if I want to.

choices.text: It gives off a somewhat lonesome feeling.
We've heard something like this before in Natlan.
What criteria did you use?

talks.objective: Return to Nasha Town and contact Varka

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... There's Varka. Oh, and it's Durin and Albedo, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Talk about coincidences. We meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, this is pretty much the same place we bumped into each other last time.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I convinced them to stick around a little longer. We were all waiting on people, so I figured having a little company would help pass the time.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah, so you've been waiting for us? Does this mean that you've already arranged things with the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sure does. Now you're back, we can go meet up with them together. How'd your investigation at the Frostmoon Enclave go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we didn't find out Columbina's true name... but apart from that, it went pretty well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We learned some stories from her early days.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Aha, just as well that I didn't tag along, then. I'm sure our Moon Goddess wouldn't want every man and his dog knowing all about her private life... Still, desperate times, desperate measures, I guess. Someone had to do it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Varka was waiting on us — but what about you two? Are you waiting for Alice?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh, no. We already met with her.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We discussed that experiment I mentioned to you last time. Oh, and she also handed me this communication device.

choices.text: This looks familiar.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: That's right. I understand she informed you about the relationship between the phantom phenomena and Teyvat's borders, yes? She wants me to help her with some more experiments on that front.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: She said that she'll contact me through this device with more information.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ah, I see. Following instructions and making observations — pretty common research method. Takes me right back to Albedo's lab...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then who exactly are you meeting?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Someone you know. Albedo's met him, too. But I don't think Miss Lauma or the Grand Master have been introduced...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Introductions are overrated — especially in cases like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's you!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: So? It's not like the Akademiya has prohibitions against going abroad. Also, I applied for leave.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I've been writing to Hat Guy since obtaining a human form. I've already brought him up to speed on everything that's been going on in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Varka & Lauma
response.text: Hat Guy...

response.speaker: Varka & Lauma
response.text: Hat Guy...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Hmph...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Turns out I actually have heard that name before.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Oh... Then, why did you react the same way I did?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, I only knew the name, not the fella! But since we're all here, let's do some introductions for what it's worth. I'm Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Lauma, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: And I'm a Driyosh from the Vahumana Darshan of the Sumeru Akademiya... Hat Guy.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Good to see you again, Mr. Guy. I believe we last saw each other on the boat ride here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So they came to Nod-Krai together...)

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Mmm. Mind you, the only reason I came here is because there's someone I want to look into.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who's that?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: The Doctor, also known as Dottore. Second of the Fatui Harbingers.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Just as I thought...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: From the tone of your voice... it sounds like there is bad blood between you.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: ...I was reviewing our archives and noticed that a lot of information about him was missing. Left a bad taste in my mouth. That's all there is to it.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Dottore... or Zandik as he was then known, once studied at the Akademiya. But he got kicked out before he could graduate.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hahahaha! So the harbingers' number two man is a college dropout? How embarrassing for them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Last we heard, he was planning something... We actually heard that a few times before even coming to Nod-Krai. But we haven't seen a trace of him since we got here.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: He only appears when something interests him. For all we know, he might have left already.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: But the fact that he did something here at all is worth noting... It'll fill a couple extra lines in his file.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Heh, why does it sound less like a file you're writing, and more like a criminal record...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Anyway, we were just about to meet two of the other Harbingers. Wanna come along? You might learn a thing or two about him there.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though they're Harbingers, uh... Well, they're old acquaintances of ours, so... y'know, when you talk to them, try to be...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Hmph. I got it.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The Frostmoon Scions' relations with the Fatui remain tense. Forgive me if I do not attend.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In that case, we'll continue assisting Ms. Alice with her experiments.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Good stuff, everyone's having a fruitful time! Alright, we'd better get going — I'll lead the way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Hey, {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you here for revenge?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Well yeah, that's obviously part of it. But I'm not the only one who has a score to settle with him.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Neither you, nor Lesser Lord Kusanali, nor I want to see him meddling with things again.

choices.text: Fair enough. One other thing...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Hah. What's the hurry?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Don't worry. Pigeons always know which way home is.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Zandik? I've heard that name before... Back in the ruins, when the Ibis King mentioned that student — that was The Doctor?)

choices.text: When we return, let's talk about Columbina.
I'm sure I saw one of these back on the Golden Apple Archipelago...

talks.objective: Go to meet with the Fatui Harbingers

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You made it... Who is this?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #A scholar from Sumeru. They call him Hat Guy. He's an old friend of {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, THIS is the Akademiya representative you wrote about? He doesn't exactly look the part...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: I believe this will prove my identity. You'll notice it bears the seal of the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well, what do you know. So it does... Alright then. My mistake.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: It's fine. I expected as much.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ahem! So, as I mentioned in my letter, the Akademiya's got its eyes on Dottore.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But this matter remains top secret. Apart from those assisting in the investigation, the fewer people who know, the better.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: If anyone asks, I am here in Nod-Krai to pursue my personal academic interests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gotta say, Varka, you did pretty well to keep all this under wraps for so long. Sounds like you got in touch with the Akademiya about this way back.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, you flatter me.

choices.text: You're all harbingers...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Where do I even start? Hmph, remember that time we fought Rerir at Starsand Shoal? He sure let me have it then, didn't he? I'll bet Dottore had that all sketched out, with me as his convenient little pawn.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: He could not care less about us if he tried. But hey, the feeling's mutual.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Does Dottore really strike you as the sort who values his relationships with his colleagues?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fair point. Definitely not.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Which is why I always keep my guard up whenever he starts making suspicious moves. To that extent, our motivations align — on top of which, I consider you trustworthy people.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Now, back on topic. In the wake of the Rächer of Solnari episode, Sandrone and I grew suspicious about Dottore's complete inaction during the entire affair. So we tried to find out what he'd been up to — but unfortunately, to no avail.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: He never lets anyone in on his plans. The more he cares about something, the more secretive he gets.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Indeed. Perhaps he believes that by keeping a low profile, he can avoid trouble. But that trick isn't going to work on his colleagues.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Yeah, I mean... He's been researching the Ancient Moon's Remnants, and he's been trying to get his paws on the Moon Marrows... Only an idiot would believe he doesn't have something more planned.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: With this in mind, I returned to Snezhnaya and relayed my thoughts to Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, entreating her to have him recalled.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's pretty direct. Did the Tsaritsa agree?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Yes. I made it abundantly clear that the Fatui's business in Nod-Krai is almost concluded, and we do not need three Harbingers in this territory. Her Majesty concurred.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Accordingly, Dottore has returned at her orders. I imagine he is continuing with experiments which no one besides he would ever have any interest in.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Common sense might mean nothing to him, but he's not stupid. He knows that no good can come from opposing the Tsaritsa.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Smarts alone won't get him all the way. He needs The Rooster's resources and Regrator's Mora — both of which the Tsaritsa can strip from him by waggling a finger.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: But doesn't he have a track record of publicly following orders while going against them in private? He probably has it down to a fine art by now.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Wouldn't put it past him... We worked together on a research project once. Only briefly, but it was enough to show me that we're fundamentally different people.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: He has no interest in doing things methodically, stage by stage. His thoughts jump all over the place, and the moment his curiosity is satisfied or he gets the results he wants, he disappears...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The only similarity we share is that, once we set our minds on doing something, we will see it done, whatever it takes.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: We definitely saw some of that in your battle with Rerir. You got so competitive...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Ugh, do NOT remind me!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Then I believe we all concur: Dottore will not simply give up.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Tch. Fantastic, now this is turning into a whole day of unpleasant memories. Ugh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you talking about the Moon Marrow stuff?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: He also strikes me as the kind of person to disregard experimental regulations, ruin all the equipment, and go way over budget... then leave the first person he can find to deal with the fallout.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Exactly! This one time, he was running some high-temperature experiment and the substance exploded. But does he care? No! He orders his subordinates to open the device so he can observe the results — which causes the gas inside to leak out...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: That gas was poisonous! If I hadn't been there, who knows how many people might've died?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And after all that? He left, while I was still cleaning up after his mess. "What a waste of time," he said.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Waste of time!? The nerve! HE wasted MY time!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, you've been bottling that up for a while, huh?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Hat Guy, I must say — you seem awfully familiar with internal Fatui affairs... especially when it comes to Dottore.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: Thank you, Lady Harbingers, for providing such valuable information. I have no other questions for now, so I'll be on my way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what? You're just gonna leave!?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
response.text: You're welcome to join if you want.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh. Just when Paimon thought he'd finally mellowed out...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: He makes quite the impression.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I'll say. I've met tons of headstrong people, but not many of them would join me in badmouthing Dottore...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Anyway, back to the main agenda. Varka, you said that Columbina has gone missing? Or rather, "disappeared"?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yeah. We're working on building a connection between her and this world. The simplest method is to find out her real name.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I've actually asked her that question before, but she said she didn't know. Considering our relationship, I doubt she was lying to me.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (We'd only just met. Even if I knew, I wouldn't have told you...)

choices.text: She could have just given you a pseudonym...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As far as I recall, she was never dispatched by Her Majesty to claim a Gnosis or anything like that.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: The Tsaritsa's plans had long contained a place specifically for her.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I always thought that was weird. What could she do that the rest of us couldn't?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Knowing what we do now, it's probably something related to kuuvahki, right?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: More than likely. When she first arrived, Columbina would often go to Her Majesty and ask when she could start the task assigned to her.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But Her Majesty always gave the same reply: "The time has not yet come." So she spent her days in Snezhnaya doing basically nothing.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: "The Tsaritsa has summoned a beautiful blind maiden to be a Harbinger, giving her the third seat by virtue only of her enchanting voice."

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: It was a dumb and stupid rumor. But the reality of the situation made it hard to refute.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And what happened after that?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I imagine she stopped caring.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: She no longer seemed to care why she had been recruited, and Her Majesty never gave her any missions, so she just... continued to sing in the flower garden.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: For my part, I was busy — so busy, in fact, that watching someone be that idle had me fuming. But still, I got the sense that...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...That she had long been used to a life of other people claiming she was needed when she wasn't.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (I... just felt that having a place to stay would cost me something eventually.)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (And so I waited quietly for the day that I would have to pay the price...)

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: *sigh* And on the other end of that spectrum, you had me. Someone once told me that I had "the lousiest work and the toughest luck." Heh, that's a good way of putting it.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I forget who said it... But those words have always stuck with me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(Sounds like something {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]} would say... No wonder.)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (But you've done your job exceptionally well all this time. Because at heart, you are a conscientious person.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for telling us all this.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: What is it? Something come to mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's nothing. I'm just even more eager to learn her name now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I want to shout it to her from the rooftops.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hehe, that makes sense. Nothing screams "you are needed!" like your name shouted from across the town.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Well, good luck with it. But if you ask me, "Columbina" is still the most shoutable name.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I'm just so used to it now, after all the arguments we've had. I can't be bothered trying to remember another name for her.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Nor I.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: (Sandrone... Arlecchino...)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You chat further about interesting moments from Columbina's past. But soon, the time comes for you to part.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, it's a Seelie! Does that mean Nicole has news for us?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ladies, I thank you for your hospitality. If the chance ever comes up, I definitely owe you both a drink sometime.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I'm sure it will.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You can make your own way out. Heck, you've been here enough times, you probably know your way around better than I do.

choices.text: Take care, everyone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, time to do what adventurers do best — follow that Seelie!

choices.text: We'll be in touch if the situation changes.
What did she do while she was with the Fatui?
What reason would you have to disclose information about Dottore?

talks.objective: Exchange intel and assess the situation

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Here you are.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Ah, Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: How come you're back so soon? Did things go alright with the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Fine. Dottore's been summoned home by the Tsaritsa. Couldn't get much more than that.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: How about you? Any progress with the investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Unfortunately not...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: We've tried everything. Different phantoms, different locations, different points in history, but the results are the same each time.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Abyssal monsters roaming the land, people crying out in despair, with no hope of being rescued.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Every time I see it, I can't help but think... is this what it was like in Mondstadt when Dragonspine-Durin attacked?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: And... if I fail in the task I've been given... will I create yet another tragedy?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...That's just meaningless speculation.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: When we encountered similar phenomena previously, I tried to interfere with those illusions, using sounds and lights to guide them.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: However, we could not change their fates. At most, we were able to extend their existences.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The events of the past are like fate that has been written into Irminsul. There isn't a living thing in Teyvat that can escape its past...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But Ms. Alice instructed us to try to find ways to change the outcome that these phantoms face.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's an impossible task. Can't you just refuse?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Since she asked us to do this, I feel like it can't truly be impossible. Or, if it is... Well, mages can make the impossible possible.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I could not have been born as "Durin" otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But you also said that your past thirty-nine attempts were fruitless.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But you're still going?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: After this many futile attempts, surely you realize that you're not doing this because you still believe what some mage told you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's because you want her hypothesis to come true. It's something you wish for deep inside.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So, think for yourself about what you want to do. As long as you don't believe it's futile, it isn't.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Previous experience indicates that we cannot touch the phantoms, which limits the effectiveness of our interventions.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If we want to clear this hurdle, we need to break this rule somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Same thought here. Following the same rules means repeating the same failures — reducing ourselves to mere playthings of fate.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So you mean... we need to figure out a way to make contact with them, despite knowing that we can't?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Yes. And I suspect that's something only you are capable of.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Everything in Teyvat is logged in Irminsul, but The Withering that once occurred in Sumeru was a sign that that great world tree was being corrupted.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This corruption allowed things that should not have existed in Teyvat to appear... This is tantamount to rewriting reality to an extent.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You're saying, Abyssal power might be able to affect these phantoms?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No one's ever tried it before. If you're gonna try it, it'll take courage, and you have to be confident that you can control it.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Is anyone there!? Has anyone seen my daughter...?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: She's missing. I... I have to find her...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I hear someone inside... Spargana? Are you in there?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Aaaargh!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: If I can use my Abyssal powers to warn him that there is danger here... maybe it'll change his decision. Maybe he'll stay away.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. The important thing is not the nature of the power, but rather how you use it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: To intimidate and obstruct... Hmph. Sounds about right for the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Let me try. I should be able to influence that thing.

talks.objective: Make use of the stone pillar to aid Razmaspes
Make use of the stone pillars to aid Razmaspes

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: He... He really left! We did it!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Don't celebrate too soon. Follow him, see what he does next.

talks.objective: Make it possible for Razmaspes to pass through
Make it possible for Razmaspes to pass through

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: The barrier's gone too. How odd...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Anyway, I guess I'll keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Quickly, let's keep up.

talks.objective: Make use of explosives to aid Razmaspes

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Perhaps I could ask for volunteers among the Frostmoon Scions.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'll see about talking to some trusted Lightkeeper colleagues. Illuga springs to mind.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: In fact, I think we had some former Frostmoon Scions join our ranks recently.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Can you gimme the scientific explanation for how the test works? I can probably make some kind of test-bot.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Then, we can just zip through Nasha Town, going up to people and pressing a button to check their status. Wouldn't that be way easier?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, no elaboration for once!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
