dialogues.text: How about I contact the Knights of Favonius garrison in the Wavechaser Plain? Shame that Lohen's already left. That guy's even tougher than I am...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Strange... The moon goddess is clearly revered by many people, so why is she on the brink of disappearing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She mentioned that the world has rejected her from the very beginning...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And when we fought the Rächer of Solnari, it seemed like she exhausted her power for our sake...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, Paimon's not sure "revered" is the right word for how people feel about her.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Gratitude, certainly. For my part, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's basic reciprocity. She helped us, so she deserves our help in return.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah, even though she looked like she didn't care... She still saved a ton of people — including me.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: A review of the relevant data leads me to conclude that Miss Columbina is a good person.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Yup, you bet!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (They really think so...?)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'm super surprised that "Columbina" isn't her actual name, though. I think it really suits her. It's light and graceful, and... yeah, just a really pretty name!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I know, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, that's not our decision to make.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ("Columbina"... That was the codename the Fatui gave me. But it also came up in the song I heard when I was born...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (But... is that really all there is to it? What do I truly think of my own name...?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is there anyone left who will still call me by that name?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...She told me to pick whichever name took my fancy. Why did I pick "Columbina"?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe because I felt that she never wanted to become Kuu{RUBY#[S]The Moon Maiden}tar, and be worshiped as a god...)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Moon-Prayer Night is getting closer by the day. We're running out of time. We need to look for other candidates.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Then allow me to try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You contacted your friends via the Adventurers' Guild. Sandrone has been keeping an eye out for something like that, so she informed me.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Since I have the ability to accommodate a Moon Marrow, I should prove to be a suitable candidate.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Arlecchino...)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: When can we begin?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I see... We can begin right away.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: How was it? Did you feel any discomfort?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: None at all.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Then it seems we shan't need to look for additional candidates after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Cool. Alright, like Paimon said, the rest of us can take turns making sure the three of 'em stay warm and comfy.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Then my job is to take care of the caretakers. I will ensure everyone receives food and accommodation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's do this. No time to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm ready as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The work is done, the sacred scroll shut. The stars grow dim, the people silent. The white sun sets, the silver moon rises. O path to the temple, appear now before us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it really opened!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (So that's what all this is about. They've been trying to open this gate...)

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: With a calm mind, this proved not too arduous. Come, let us enter.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: It might be best to eat something first. Take care to chew properly and swallow slowly. It will give your body time to readjust to the digestion process.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (They will head in soon.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (They will need to enter this gate...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I... cannot pass through. Is it because I have no physical body?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ugh... Aah...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (It has been three days... My strength has all but completely faded...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Can I really... hold on until Moon-Prayer Night...?)

talks.objective: Make use of explosives to aid Razmaspes

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: So many... monsters...!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: There's still a chance, Durin. Use the traps.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: ...Which is why we need a lantern guaranteed to work on the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. I have a few ideas, but... The lantern itself is the easy part. The real issue is how little we know about the lunar environment.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wait... you two are serious about this?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hehe. Let's just say I'm intrigued by these shining magical stones that Mr. Albedo has mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: This is a new development... I've never seen this happen before...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: We might just be able to save this person.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Hello there... Have you seen my daughter? Spargana's her name. She's carrying a large backpack...

dialogues.speaker: Gaoramus
dialogues.text: ...Get out while you still can, you fool... You won't find any survivors here...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: But I can't just leave her here. She must be so scared right now...

dialogues.speaker: Gaoramus
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...Sorry, wish I could help, but I haven't seen her. You'll just have to keep looking.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Okay. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: If I do find her, I'll get her to shelter and come back for you.

dialogues.speaker: Gaoramus
dialogues.text: Don't bother. I've got nowhere left to go.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: What's that noise...?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: M—Monster... Aaaaahhh!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...If he goes inside, he'll be walking into a trap. Let's try this once more — this time, we have to stop him.

talks.objective: Wait for Razmaspes to gather information

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: H—Hello, I'm looking for... Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Phryazantus
dialogues.text: Looking for what? Everything here belongs to me!

dialogues.speaker: Phryazantus
dialogues.text: Get him, boys!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Aghhh!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Huh? That's... That looks like one of my daughter's books!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you, thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Yes, it's one of hers for sure — there's her name on it, right there! She left her backpack here.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Durin, just like last time! Use the explosives!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are you out for a walk too?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The day has come at last...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: That's my daughter's book! She's passed this way! Why... Why won't you let me go in!?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I've searched, and searched, and searched... just for this! But how will I find her without any clues!?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I no longer have anywhere else to go...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It won't work... there's not enough left. If he makes it in, he'll die.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But then... This clue could be the key to him finding his daughter...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It might not be the only one. Better he misses that clue than loses his life.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I guess so...

talks.objective: Block the gate ahead of Razmaspes

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I'm so sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: He refuses to go anywhere else... Whether he opens this door or not, all that awaits him now is death. We... couldn't change his fate.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Albedo, Hat Guy, let's try one more time. I don't know how we're going to do this, but I don't want to give up either.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Why am I here... What's going on? All these scenes running through my head... Where are they from?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: His reactions have changed.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: How many times have I... What's happening to me? I—I...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Huh. Wait. Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Y—You can see us now?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I... feel like I always could, but that I only just "realized" you were there... I'm sorry. I don't know how to describe what I'm feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: But... You were the ones guiding me using that marked barrier, right?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I haven't done anything yet, but those monsters, those deaths... They feel like memories. Like things I really did experience...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I... I won't find my daughter. In fact, I'll ultimately die trying to find her. Isn't that right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wh... No, it isn't.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Yes, it is.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Even so, we're trying to find a way out of this.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: You've not seen my daughter either, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: It seems she really isn't here...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Ugh... Oh... Ohh...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry we couldn't help you.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I'm just... tired. Maybe this is destiny. Maybe it doesn't matter how hard I search...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: How long do I have left?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Experience says fifteen to twenty minutes.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Fifteen to twenty... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Thank you for all your help. Let's rest a while. You look exhausted too...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Now's not the time for you to start pitying us.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Haha, it's not pity... I'm just... realizing that I've only got ten or so minutes left, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: You say you're from Mondstadt, yes? A place with windmills, where the people enjoy limitless freedom?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: And you're from Sumeru, where they've built an academy into a giant tree?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. It seems you've never heard of either place.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Those names are unknown to me, I'm afraid, yes. Have you heard of Hyperborea?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I have, but... I heard that it was destroyed in the distant past...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I see. That was where my ancestors once lived. What about Delphi Pytho? Was it later rebuilt?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've never heard that name.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Then what about Sal Vindagnyr?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I have seen that name on stone tablets on Dragonspine, but I'm afraid the only things left of that place are its ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I see... Sure enough, there was no way to turn this around, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm sorry. I was the one who asked to chat, but it seems like we're too many ages apart. There's barely any common ground to start from.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's alright. We did hear something new, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: From how you speak of your lives, things must be going alright for you, I guess?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: They are. Mondstadt is a place of freedom and happiness. There's a lot of good people in the Church and the Knights of Favonius, and even outsiders find that it's an easy place to feel at home.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: We have festivals a few times a year... everyone gets together to drink, sing, and be merry...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Sumeru's a lot more uptight. Not really the kind of place where you can relax. It's a nation fraught with problems wherever you look.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: But if all you want in life is to seek knowledge, I guess it's pretty much paradise.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: That's wonderful.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: In other words, after this all-devouring black tide passed, humanity did not merely avoid extinction, but rose to build prosperous civilizations anew.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: I mean, I can see you all right now. That must mean the future isn't a total mess, right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...That's true.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Well, time's almost up. Let's part ways, I think. Might be best if you don't waste too much time on me.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: The chances are slim, I know, but I'd like to spend these last few minutes looking for Spargana. If things work out, I'd love to tell her about all that I've heard.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: May we meet again... Well, or not, most probably... In that case, may your wishes come true.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: He's gone. In a few minutes, he will meet the end that was his to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The ending of this tale did not change, but I believe that we've just made the most progress we have yet.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: "May your wishes come true"... If only it were so simple.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hat Guy, could I ask you a question?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You've never talked about your past. It seems complicated... and it weighs heavily on you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Would you be willing to tell me about it? I mean, sometimes it's better to get things out in the open. Take that guy we tried to help, for instance — at least he said goodbye with a smile, right?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I know about Albedo's past. Our experiences are very similar, and he created me.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: As for you, you're my first friend, and you've witnessed every step I've taken. But by comparison, I know nothing about you.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Either way, I mean, we're still best friends! But... if I knew more about you, I might understand your thoughts a bit better...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: I've told you about myself. I'm a student at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: And what did you do before that?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Prepared for the entrance exam.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Alright. If you really don't want to talk about it, I won't press you any further.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I was a puppet bu{RUBY#[D]Simulanka}ilt from the branches of a white tree, using technology left behind by the Khaenri'ahn schools of mechanical engineering.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A white tree? You mean an Irminsul tree?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Yes. A branch of Irminsul that was once connected to the main tree.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So you had a human creator too...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Yeah. But my creator abandoned me after deciding that I was a failure.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: After that...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Durin, resisting the influence of the Abyss, suppressing the urge to destroy, trying to do the right thing... None of these things are easy.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: But no matter how hard they are, trying to rewrite past wrongs is far harder.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: You asked me if you would create a new tragedy if you failed. I told you there was no point speculating about that.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: But the real answer is... Yes. You absolutely will.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hat Guy...

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: But at least you've got people here to help steer you away from the wrong path. So... just keep aiming towards the light.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I will. I promise.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}
dialogues.text: Alright. Break time's over.

dialogues.speaker: Dodocommunication Device
dialogues.text: Dodo!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hello? Durin speaking...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hello friends, it's me. What have you been up to, hmm? I'm detecting some unmistakable fluctuations here at the border.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The amplitude isn't particularly high, but they're completely different signals from the ones before. And the scale is comparable to those I've detected previously.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Alice, we were unable to save that person. However, he appears to have retained a portion of the memories gained through that cycle, and was able to hold a conversation with us.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I see... Well, that is rather odd indeed. It definitely merits further attention.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Could I trouble you to keep trying the same approach? I need to gather some more data. Counting on you~!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, I should probably have Nicole come and check this out as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: There you are. I was worried you might stop to collect treasure chests opened by the Seelie along the way... It would have taken you so much longer to get here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (*sigh*... Another conversation I cannot hear...)

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I am delighted to see that you understand what takes priority, and that your adventurer's instinct has not swayed your resolve. Really, I must applaud you for it... You should know—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Agh, Paimon's head...)

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...Okay, I'll try and keep it short... My senses are telling me that this is where we shall find the entrance to the ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, cool. Well, what are we waiting for? Let's open it up and see!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Patience. This was a sanctuary of great importance to the Hyperboreans. A special process is required to open the gate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... like the place that housed the Eternal Moon's Marrow?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like the ancients were very fond of making tricky gate puzzles...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Mkay, so what's the plan? Need us to do anything? ...Uh, and just the short version, if you can!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ah. Alright then. I was planning to start with some background on the invention of these techniques... Are you sure you don't want to hear it? It's quite informative.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Remember what you were saying about priorities...?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Fine. Simply put, we need three human representatives to successfully undergo a process of kuuvahki resonance.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Think of it as a test from the three moon goddesses to see if the entrants are qualified, with the most recognizable qualification being kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pretty sure Lauma would ace that test! ...Oh, wait, but we need three people...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I also have no doubt that the Moonchanter would be qualified. But we would need two other people with the same constitution.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Therefore, the most feasible method is not so much to follow the rules, but to figure out how the test functions and find a workaround.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I've done some research, and it turns out the mechanism is rather crude. We'll simply need humans to stand before it who have sufficient kuuvahki energy within them.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm with you so far. How do we get the kuuvahki in them?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hmm... The easiest way would be transfusion. Take some kuuvahki from Nod-Krai's soil, put it into the bloodstream, and get it circulating in the body.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So, we're going to... cheat on the test?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Precisely. There are other methods, but this is the simplest one. Cheating the system is much easier than trying to hide from it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sorry? Does the idea of cheating upset you, Miss Lauma?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...No, that's not it. I just... I suddenly had an idea!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It's about Moon-Prayer Night. I've figured out a way for Kuutar to join in the festivities!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But as Paimon said, we need to have our priorities straight. Let's get back to the test — I'll follow up with Nefer on the festival arrangements.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, okay. Anyway, is this really the best method we have? A kuuvahki transfusion sounds dangerous, no matter how you slice it...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If you think that's dangerous, wait till you hear the other methods... I'd be more than happy to go through them if you'd like? There are several—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No need! We're good! Let's go with this one!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Very well. Kuuvahki transfusion it is. Now, I should mention that the risks can be greater or lower depending on individual compatibility.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It would be rash to simply infuse the kuuvahki and hope for the best. If the body rejects it, the reaction can be quite severe.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The symptoms are similar to another condition that some people living here suffer from, known as congenital kuuvahki sensitivity.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: So, before we execute our plan, I will perform a simple test of my own to see who is compatible, and who is not.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Once that is done, we will have to complete the resonance process as rapidly as possible. The participants must remain stationary while the kuuvahki circulates and bonds with them, and they mustn't eat or drink anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? No eating or drinking?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That's some hardcore fasting... They'll all be monks by the time they're through.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How long will they have to keep that up?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Three days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's so long! And we still need to find two more people who are not just compatible, but also willing to volunteer...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Fasting...? What are they talking about...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm willing to volunteer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Don't you wanna think this through?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, count me in, too. Three days without food? I can handle that.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ms. Nicole has made it clear that this is the easiest way. The way I see it, there's nothing else to discuss. It's time to step up.

choices.text: Compared to having Columbina disappear completely...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. You're right. I—In that case, Paimon volunteers to be captain of logistics! She'll keep the fires lit and grab some spare clothes to keep you comfortable!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Good work, Paimon.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: #Then we'll start with you first, {NICKNAME}. Please step forward.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: How is it going? Do you feel anything?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: How about now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: And now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still nothing.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Huh... Wh—What about now?

choices.text: Nothing at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You guys... it's not a competition, you know...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Alright, I'm officially impressed. Even as a Descender, you can withstand far more than I imagined...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It's like I summoned a giant stone titan to arm wrestle you, and your arm hasn't even moved an inch.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: In my last attempt, I infused five times the amount of kuuvahki required.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That much!?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Yes. Safe to say, compatibility won't be an issue for you. You're eligible to join.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: You're next, Mr. Varka.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sure. Here goes nothing.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Alright. I'll start where we left off — five times the required kuuvahki dose...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Whoa whoa whoa, hey, hey, wait a minute...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ugh... Ugh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... How's it going?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: N—Not great, I uh... kinda wanna puke. Feels like I've been drinking too much... a few bottles of wine, then a big stein of "Dark Horse"... with some hard liquor from Liyue mixed in...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Hehe.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You think this is funny? I just lost to a young lady in an arm-wrestling contest. I'm never gonna live that down!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: My apologies. I'll lower the concentration and try again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How's it going now?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'm not as dizzy as last time, but I can still feel it pulsing around.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: In that case, you wouldn't be an ideal choice, Mr. Varka. Let's try someone else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, let's go ask some of our other friends, then!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: No surprises here, Miss Moonchanter. You're perfectly compatible. You may join.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I'm getting a slight headache.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Shame. You were so close.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Whoa, I—I'm itching all over...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Allergic reaction. We can't have that.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Well? Are you gonna start or what?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The Hexenzirkel is an organization that cares for and protects children. We will not have them do dangerous things — not even tests.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Is something the matter?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The candidates have to be human.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: (I guess that rules me out too.)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Huh, everyone except the Moonchanter got beaten. Guess I don't need to feel so bad after all... Ahem, uh, I mean, looks like this isn't gonna be as easy as we thought.

choices.text: Did you do something?
...Fasting for a few days is nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Miss Lauma, would you accompany me into town? I think it'd be best if you saw the Frostmoon Scions' decorations for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Very well. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Hello there. I'm looking for my daughter. She carries a large backpack. Have you seen her?

dialogues.speaker: Maina
dialogues.text: I did see a few young girls... None with a backpack, but surely she would've ditched it, no?

dialogues.speaker: Maina
dialogues.text: *sigh* What are you even doing here? How are you going to get back out?

dialogues.speaker: Maina
dialogues.text: Not only are there monsters, but there's explosives too... If only my legs would work properly, I'd... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: That's fine. That's all I needed to hear. Thanks for telling me.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Ugh, another monster...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Aaaaaaggghhh!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I guess we can't let him in here either.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Aaaargh!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: #After leaving the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]} goes to meet Durin and Albedo, who are observing the phantoms.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Could you do me a solid and try to smooth things over with Boss Nef?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The phantom has met its end and returned to his place of origin.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once, long ago, The Damselette who lived here walked the line between dreams and reality.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After leaving the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, The Balladeer heads straight to where Durin and Albedo were.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The rescue has reached a dead end. All that can be done is to wait for another chance.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After the conversation ends, the group splits into two teams. Led by Varka, you make it safely into the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: This may be your last chance to visit the Frostmoon Enclave. Don't let it slip away.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Maybe it's not so bad, just quietly staying by their side like this...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: (Time is of the essence. I can't stray too far from him.)

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Have you seen a little girl?

dialogues.speaker: Vayutana
dialogues.text: What!? This isn't the time for that! Just run!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Wh—What is this!? Looks dangerous... I should get out of here...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Aaaargh!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: H—Help me...!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Ah!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Monsters approaching from the front. You need to stop them and create an opportunity for him to hide.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: No, there's a monster ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Wait, is that the barrier I saw earlier? Why is it appearing now... It's as if someone's controlling it...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: The monster's gone... Is it safe now?

dialogues.speaker: Atarfarnes
dialogues.text: Wait, there was someone else here? Don't go any further, we've got anti-monster traps laid out everywhere!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: But, my daughter must just be up ahead. I have to go...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: We might be able to use the explosives over there, but we need to take care not to hurt him.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'll use the barrier to keep him at a safe distance.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: This barrier... seems to be helping me somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: No good. Gotta keep moving ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Wh—Why? How will I know where Spargana's gone like this...?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: ...You know what? I'll trust this strange barrier. It's gotten me this far, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: Wait, no entry here either!?

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: A—Alright then...

dialogues.speaker: Phryazantus
dialogues.text: What!? What's this? Hey, let us out!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Stop him, Durin. We can't let him get any further in.

dialogues.speaker: Fleeing Person B
dialogues.text: The monsters are coming!

dialogues.speaker: Fleeing Person C
dialogues.text: Ah! Someone help me!

dialogues.speaker: Fleeing Person D
dialogues.text: I—I don't want to die!

dialogues.speaker: Injured Person A
dialogues.text: What do we do... We can't get away...

dialogues.speaker: Injured Person B
dialogues.text: Where are all these monsters coming from...

dialogues.speaker: Injured Person C
dialogues.text: If this goes on... We're gonna die...

dialogues.speaker: Razmaspes
dialogues.text: No, no, no, I can't die here... Aaaahhh!
